newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius stocks start new year quietly upward.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius stocks start new year quietly upward.

text.p: Stocks on the Mauritian bourse had a featureless start for 1997 in a quiet Monday in which the market index edged up 0.54 points to 354.00, brokers said.
Volume totalled 6.11 million rupees on 237,710 shares from 18.98 million rupees on 686,587 shares last Monday.
The Mauritian bourse official market, which trades on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays, was closed last Wednesday and Friday for the New Year festivities.

Moving shares ended mixed with the market seen as stable, brokers said. "As expected, investors are not particularly active at the start of the year. Things can remain like that for quite some time," one broker said.
Mauritius Commercial Bank was unchanged at 80 rupees on 13,485 shares and State Bank of Mauritius was stable at 10.30 rupees on 41,200 shares.
Mauritius Oil Refineries gained 30 cents to 10.30 rupees on 4,000 shares and building materials manufacturer United Basalt Products was 50 cents up to 33.10 rupees on 1,978 shares.
Consolidated Investment Trust (CIT) was unchanged at 10 rupees on 22,850 shares and Mauritius Development Investment Trust (MDIT) was 10 cents up to 8.30 rupees on 26,900 shares.
Conglomerate Rogers rose 1.50 rupees to 90.50 rupees on 12,063 shares while Happy World Foods lost 50 cents to 16.50 rupees with 3,700 shares on ex-dividend trading on Monday.
Oil company Shell (Mauritius) was 10 cents lower to 13.90 rupees on 1,000 shares and national carrier Air Mauritius slipped 50 cents to 44.50 rupees on 1,850 shares.
